raw_response:
Answer: C
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates bilateral, patchy, peripheral airspace opacities (consolidation) which, combined with a two-month history of fever and dry cough, is the classic radiographic and clinical presentation of Cryptogenic Organizing Pneumonia (COP). This pattern distinguishes it from lobar pneumonia (typically unilateral/segmental), tuberculosis (often apical/cavitary), or pulmonary edema (central/perihilar distribution).
